seo.og_description: Discover Morocco's Blue Pearl: top sights, authentic guesthouses, Akchour waterfalls, and travel tips.

hero_subtitle: Morocco's iconic Blue Pearl shining in the heart of the stunning Rif Mountains.

overview.title: Welcome to the Blue Pearl
overview.p1: World-famous for its striking palette of blue-washed buildings nestled in the dramatic Rif Mountains, Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 as a fortress. This peaceful mountain town offers a relaxing refuge from the hustle of the major Imperial cities.
overview.p2: Wander through cobblestone winding alleys, relax in vibrant squares over mint tea, watch the sunset over the valley from the Spanish Mosque, or embark on nature trails in Talassemtane National Park.

places.title: Top Attractions in Chefchaouen
places.subtitle: Iconic blue alleys, historic fortresses, and breathtaking mountain views.

outa.title: Outa el-Hammam Square
outa.desc: The vibrant heart of the city surrounded by outdoor cafes, dominated by the red-walled Kasbah and the Grand Mosque.

kasbah.title: Chefchaouen Kasbah
kasbah.desc: A 15th-century fortress featuring lush Andalusian gardens, an ethnographic museum, and a tower with panoramic views.

akchour.title: Akchour Waterfalls & Bridge of God
akchour.desc: Stunning river trails, emerald natural pools, and dramatic rock arches in Talassemtane National Park.

mosquee.title: Spanish Mosque (Bouzaafar)
mosquee.desc: A hilltop mosque offering the best sunset view over the blue city and the surrounding valley.

medina.title: Medina Blue Alleys
medina.desc: The famous maze of blue-painted walls, vibrant doors, and narrow streets perfect for photography.

bab_ain.title: Bab El Ain
bab_ain.desc: One of the main historic gates of the Medina, an ideal starting point to explore the blue quarters.

talassemtane.title: Talassemtane National Park
talassemtane.desc: A protected nature reserve featuring fir forests, dramatic peaks, and scenic hiking trails.

haouta.title: El Haouta Square
haouta.desc: A charming small square inside the Medina featuring an ancient zellige fountain and a peaceful atmosphere.

ras_maa.title: Ras El Maa Spring
ras_maa.desc: A refreshing mountain spring outside the Medina walls where watermills turn and locals come to unwind.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced schedule for snapping the best photos and enjoying mountain experiences.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start your tour in the main square, visit the Kasbah and its gardens, then stroll through the blue alleys when the light is gentle and streets are quiet.
detailed_itinerary.day1_a: Afternoon — Getting Lost in the Alleys
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Take your time exploring the Medina's pathways, stopping at small shops and cafes. Enjoy mint tea in the square and keep your camera ready around every corner.
detailed_itinerary.day1_e: Evening — Sunset at the Spanish Mosque
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Hike up to the Spanish Mosque for panoramic views over the blue rooftops at sunset, then head back down for dinner in the Medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Catch a grand taxi early towards Akchour for a scenic river walk through Talassemtane National Park, up to the small waterfall or the Bridge of God trail if you have energy.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Head back to town in the afternoon and sample the region's famous goat cheese, served with fresh bread and local olives.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: End your day with a traditional dinner on a rooftop terrace overlooking the lights of the Medina.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Walk to the Ras El Maa spring at the edge of the Medina, where locals gather, wash clothes, and relax near the fresh water.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit local weavers and craft shops to see handwoven blankets, wool products, and artisanal crafts made right by the artisans.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Savor one last cup of mint tea in the square before heading to your next destination.

stays.title: Where to Stay in Chefchaouen? Our Favorites
stays.subtitle: From luxury riads with spas to charming boutique hotels on mountain slopes, here are the best places to stay.

card1.name: Lina Ryad & Spa
card1.desc: An exceptional luxury riad featuring indoor pools, upscale spa facilities, and elegant rooms overlooking the blue city.

card2.name: Dar Jasmine Boutique Hotel
card2.desc: A gorgeous hillside boutique hotel featuring a pool, lush gardens, and breathtaking panoramic views of Chefchaouen.

card3.name: Casa Perleta
card3.desc: A cozy, authentic guesthouse blending traditional Andalusian architecture with warm hospitality and a lovely terrace.

booking_banner.title: Explore all hotels and riads in Chefchaouen
booking_banner.desc: Compare live prices, read trusted guest reviews, and enjoy free cancellation on most mountain riads and stays.

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Cafes
eat.subtitle: Authentic Northern Moroccan dishes, goat cheese, and panoramic rooftop views

ssour.title: Bab Ssour
ssour.desc: A cozy multi-level restaurant serving home-style tagines, fresh salads, and local specialties.

sofia.title: Restaurant Sofia
sofia.desc: A family-run eatery famous for delicious pastilla, tagines, and warm hospitality.

aladdin.title: Restaurant Aladdin
aladdin.desc: An Arab-Andalusian palace offering panoramic views over the Kasbah from three rooftop terraces.

shoes.title: Steep Alleys & Comfortable Shoes
shoes.desc: Wear comfortable walking shoes with good grip — the cobblestone steps and blue streets can be steep and slippery.

photo.title: Photography Etiquette
photo.desc: Always ask for permission before taking close-up photos of locals, especially elders and children in the Medina.

cash.title: Cash & ATMs
cash.desc: Most small shops, cafes, and guesthouses accept cash only (Moroccan Dirham MAD). ATMs are available near Outa el-Hammam Square.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Chefchaouen
daytrips.subtitle: Discover waterfalls, national parks, and nearby coastal mountain routes.

akchour.title: Akchour Waterfalls & Bridge of God
akchour.desc: Emerald pools, river trails, and the natural rock arch of the Bridge of God (45 minutes by car).

tetouan.title: Tetouan Medina
tetouan.desc: A UNESCO-listed Andalusian medina rich in artisanal heritage (1.5 hours by car).

ouedlaou.title: Mediterranean Coast (Oued Laou)
ouedlaou.desc: Pebble beaches and turquoise waters on the Mediterranean coast (1.25 hours by car).

tanger.title: Tangier - Gateway to Africa
tanger.desc: Combine your trip with the legendary coastal city on the Strait of Gibraltar (2.25 hours by car).

q1.question: How many days should I stay in Chefchaouen?
q1.answer: Spending 2 to 3 days is ideal to explore the old medina, watch the sunset at the Spanish Mosque, and take a day trip to the Akchour Waterfalls.

q2.question: Is Chefchaouen easily accessible by train or bus?
q2.answer: No, Chefchaouen does not have a train station. The easiest options are CTM buses, grand taxis, or private transfers from Tangier, Tetouan, or Fes.

q3.question: Why is Chefchaouen painted blue?
q3.answer: There are several theories: introduced by Jewish refugees in the 1930s representing the sky, kept as a natural mosquito repellent, or to keep houses cool and attract visitors.
